items.summary: The macroscopic capabilities of intelligent systems arise from the local interactions of many simple units. When such systems are deployed in the real world, their behaviour must nevertheless be constrained, leaving designers caught between releasing adaptability and preventing loss of control, yet without formal tools to resolve the dilemma. This paper proposes a unified research program for controlled emergence that restates this tension as a pair of dual problems: the forward problem explains macroscopic behaviour from local rules, and the inverse problem solves for controllable rules and readout mechanisms from a desired target. We take an augmented quintuple as the formal object shared by both ends, and decompose ``engineering'' into three independently measurable coordinates: controllability, reproducibility, and degree of formalizability. On this basis we give three testable working hypotheses (critical scale; the cooperation and trade-off between constraint and adaptability; minimal constraint) and one feasibility criterion, which reduce inverse design from unconstrained optimization to interval checking. The program takes explicit failure boundaries as its premise, does not pursue complete control, and always preserves the system's room for self-organization. The reduced pilot experiment attached to this paper serves only to verify the executability of the research protocol and does not constitute a statistical test of the working hypotheses. This design language generalizes to multi-agent artificial intelligence, the industrial internet, and emergency response systems, all of which must confront emergence and controllability at once.
items.title: The Forward/Inverse Duality of Controlled Emergence:A Computational Design Program from Explanation to Engineering

items.summary: Geometric full-waveform inversion aims to recover sharp subsurface interfaces from noisy waveform observations. We formulate this problem within a Bayesian level-set framework, where the unknown interface is represented as zero level set of a latent function endowed with a Gaussian prior. Although the level-set-to-medium-parameter map is discontinuous, we establish that the level-set-to-observation map is continuous almost surely with respect to the prior, thereby guaranteeing that the posterior measure is well-posed and locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the data in the Hellinger metric. To enable tractable posterior computation under the severe nonlinearity of the inverse problem and the resulting multimodality, we develop a multiscale multimodal Laplace approximation. A frequency-continuation strategy incorporates waveform data progressively from low to high frequencies, identifying and propagating multiple candidate modes across successive scales. At the final frequency level, local Gaussian approximations are constructed around the retained modes and combined into a Gaussian mixture, whose weights are determined by least-squares fitting to the unnormalized posterior density. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method accurately reconstructs anomalous interfaces while effectively capturing posterior multimodality and the local uncertainty associated with distinct plausible geometries.
items.title: Bayesian Geometric Inversion for Wave Equation: Well-Posedness and Multiscale Multimodal Posterior Approximation

items.summary: Ranking data in modern applications often involves covariate vectors whose dimension grows with the number of objects. Identifying relevant covariates and integrating them with item-specific utilities can yield better predictive performance. In this work, we study a Plackett--Luce model that incorporates both item-specific utilities and high-dimensional covariate effects. Under a sparsity assumption on the covariate coefficients, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for identifiability in terms of the Kruskal rank of the restricted covariate design. We then propose an $\ell_1$-regularized maximum likelihood estimator for the covariate coefficients. Under suitable design and connectivity conditions, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the estimator with probability tending to one, as well as its uniform consistency. With an additional minimum-signal condition, we further establish exact support recovery. Our analysis combines a hypergraph-based chaining technique with a profile-likelihood perturbation analysis, yielding estimation rates that explicitly capture the effects of the comparison hypergraph's connectivity and the underlying sparsity level. Numerical experiments using synthetic data and a horse racing dataset corroborate our theoretical findings.
items.title: High-dimensional covariate-assisted ranking

items.summary: Sea level fingerprints connect the spatial distribution of rapid ice mass change to sea surface height (SSH) change, but the spatial resolving power of this inverse problem remains poorly quantified. Here we provide the first systematic, scale-resolved quantification of Greenland Ice Sheet mass change structure recoverable from its SSH fingerprint when ice loss geometry varies. We develop a physics-informed neural operator, constrained by an accurate neural-operator emulator of the forward sea level equation, to probe the information content of this ill-conditioned inverse problem. Across synthetic ice change ensembles, broad ice loss patterns can be recovered, but distinct ice fields can produce nearly identical fingerprints, so fine-scale structure depends on the assumed a-priori ice change distribution. Inversion fidelity varies with the wavelength and amplitude of ice mass change. An empirical error law separates these effects and defines a scale-dependent accuracy ceiling. For a satellite-altimetry-derived reference field, the estimated fingerprint-only ceiling is $R^2\sim0.79$ under the present SSH observation geometry and matched-prior assumption. The leading three principal components explain 99.76% of fingerprint variance, yet higher-order components retain information needed to distinguish finer ice change structure. SSH observations near Greenland carry most information on ice loss locations. Applying the leading fingerprint principal components to the observed 1993--2019 SSH rate recovers the large-scale Greenland fingerprint, while the residual field is correlated with basin-scale bathymetry, consistent with unresolved sterodynamic variability. These results establish a quantitative empirical bound on fingerprint-only ice-loss resolving power and identify how independent observations and ice sheet constraints can improve inference.
items.title: Neural Operators Reveal Scale-Dependent Limits on Recovering Greenland Ice Loss from Sea Level Fingerprints

items.summary: Image restoration is a fundamental inverse problem that seeks to recover high-quality images from degraded observations. Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods provide a flexible framework for integrating pretrained denoisers into iterative reconstruction, whereas flow matching offers an efficient generative modeling approach based on continuous-time ODE dynamics. Very recently, Martin et al.\ (ICLR, 2025) developed a PnP-Flow method, which integrates the PnP framework with flow matching through a time-dependent denoiser constructed from a pretrained flow matching model.By incorporating a different time schedule and an additional pixel-space projection operator, this paper proposes a novel efficient PnP-Flow algorithm (HP-PnP-Flow) that enjoys rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, without imposing restrictive conditions on iterates required by the aforementioned work. Numerical experiments on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat demonstrate that the newly proposed HP-PnP-Flow algorithm significantly outperforms PnP-Flow on several restoration tasks such as denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, random inpainting, and box inpainting. Notably, our algorithm achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality with substantially fewer iterations, reducing the iteration count from $500$ to $100$ for deblurring and super-resolution on AFHQ-Cat.
items.title: HP-PnP-Flow: Hybrid Time Scheduling and Projection for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration via Flow Matching

items.summary: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.
items.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability

items.summary: We study inverse coefficient problems for two evolution equations with relaxation: a Kelvin--Voigt viscoelastic equation and the Moore--Gibson--Thompson (MGT) equation arising in nonlinear acoustics. In both cases, we establish the Lipschitz stability for recovering a space-dependent coefficient from a single measurement. Our approach exploits an exact factorization of each operator into a classical evolution operator (the heat operator for the viscoelastic system, or the wave operator for the MGT equation) coupled with a first-order differential operator in time. This makes it possible to combine global Carleman estimates with weighted ODE inequalities. For the Kelvin--Voigt model, the data consist of an interior dynamic observation and a Cauchy snapshot at a prescribed positive time. For the MGT equation, a single boundary trace is sufficient under a standard geometric condition. The resulting argument provides a common framework for coefficient inverse problems in evolution equations with relaxation effects.
items.title: A unified Carleman approach to inverse problems for coupled parabolic and hyperbolic-ODE equations

items.summary: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.
items.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?

items.summary: Traditional evaluation benchmarks reduce inherently interconnected scientific knowledge in life sciences into flat lists of questions, disregarding the underlying topological structure of the knowledge. We introduce, the first graph-structured benchmark for life sciences, featuring over 10,000 high-quality multiple-choice questions across medicine, biology, and chemistry. Our approach constructs a weighted evaluation graph using bidirectional matching and semantic similarity algorithms, where nodes represent questions and edge weights capture their semantic relationships. Leveraging this graph topology, we design two novel evaluation metrics. The Global Coherence Score (GCS) measures a model's consistency within semantically related neighborhoods, while Knowledge Balance Score (KBS) analyzes how model errors are distributed across the graph to reveal conceptual blind spots. LG-Bench facilitates fine-grained comparison of LLMs by surfacing differences in conceptual coherence and patterns of knowledge organization across models. Our framework shifts the evaluation paradigm from flat accuracy metrics to structure-aware analysis, offering a new lens for diagnosing and improving LLM performance in the life sciences domain.
items.title: LG-Bench: A Graph-Structured Evaluation Benchmark for Life Sciences

items.summary: Run records, logs, analyses and binding-event replica trajectories of the streptavidin : fibril ratio sweep simulated by Team Imperial College (iGEM 2026, Imperial College London) with HyFiP-LDF, our open-source coarse-grained HOOMD-blue 7.2.0 Langevin-dynamics model of a protein hydrogel (HET-s(218–289) amyloid fibrils end-labelled with maleimide–PEG–biotin linkers and crosslinked by streptavidin tetramers). The sweep covers six streptavidin : fibril ratios (1/6, 1/4, 1/2, 1, 3/2, 3) at three random seeds each, 105 ns per run at surrogate conditions (75 nm fibrils, ten times the wet-lab number density, friction scaled by 0.1, 300 nm periodic box), run on one NVIDIA RTX 5090. 13 of 18 runs finished; the configurations and partial logs of the 5 stopped runs are included. Also included are the 52 re-simulations of one binding event (restarted from saved frames with new random seeds at 2 ps resolution) used to study how a biotin finds a streptavidin pocket. For every run: the complete resolved configuration, a run manifest with software versions and every model parameter with its provenance and data-file hashes, the HOOMD energy and temperature log, and the network, thermodynamic and structural analyses. These are the data behind Figures 26–28 and Videos 4–5 of the Simulations page of our wiki. Software: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/imperial-college/cg-langevin-simulation (Apache-2.0). Atomistic reference data: 10.5281/zenodo.23420371. See README.md inside the archive for the file layout, variables, units and methods.
items.title: Imperial College 2026 — reGELerate: HyFiP-LDF coarse-grained ratio-sweep simulations (run records, analyses and binding-event replicas)

items.summary: Assembly traces can support explicit probabilistic inference without being treated as recovered program meaning. Active Assembly Theory and Practice makes that distinction executable: transparent x86-64 fixtures are decoded with Capstone, traced under bounded Unicorn emulation, and mapped to typed observations that distinguish missing, unseen, and unsupported evidence. Two Generalized Notation Notation (GNN) specifications define passive-phase and prospective sensor models whose tensors drive real pymdp execution. A native categorical Julia/RxInfer companion consumes the passive model's same parameters (Friedman 2026; Heins et al. 2022; Bagaev et al. 2023). The sensor Agent selects an action before fixture evidence is acquired. Independent finite calculations check beliefs and policy scores; native smoothing uses the same parameters and first-observation convention. Every inference comparator and fitted diagnostic also consumes an upstream-parsed numeric GNN specification, with source-bound runtime instances and rendered model graphs. A corpus of 10 authored fixtures supports complete-fixture exclusion diagnostics. At the fixed informative likelihood, the memoryless decoder outperforms the temporal filter; temporal advantages appear under synthetic observation ambiguity. Designed category ambiguity remains a visible failure case. The separate Gaussian and categorical Bethe free-energy diagnostics are not compared numerically with policy expected free energy. The quotient benchmark contains 64 transformation-family identifiers and 4096 rows, with 16 families held out from model fitting. The co-primary portfolio includes an interpretable classifier, a temporal probabilistic model, a fixed one-layer tanh recurrent classifier, and surface baselines; the temporal endpoint reaches balanced accuracy 0.775 and macro-F1 0.772 on this frozen bounded benchmark. Held-out identifiers share authored template lineages with the fitting data. Family-resampling intervals and conditional randomization diagnostics therefore describe this finite inventory; the retrospective protocol correction withholds superiority claims. A complementary pinned static-only corpus supplies 5 licensed source projects and 100 source-contract rows, including 40 lexical witnesses, 40 contract-directed near misses, and 20 identity controls. The corpus establishes provenance and coverage; it does not execute arbitrary external binaries or support application-effectiveness claims. Selected normalized machine-state relations are checked by Python, native execution, and a bounded Lean fragment. Exact finite sensing certificates and source-bound reader artifacts make assumptions and failures inspectable. Independent physical replication remains unearned. The contribution is a reproducible substrate for testing assembly-to-inference mechanisms, with explicit limits on semantics, statistical generalization, and external validity.
items.title: Active Assembly Theory and Practice

items.summary: SSTIM Workbench , previously developed as BSC Lab, is the open reference environment for SSTIM , the Sensory Stimulation Vocabulary developed through the W3C Sensory Stimulation Vocabulary Community Group . It has two integrated layers: a precision multi-engine audiovisual stimulation application, and a knowledge layer over the SSTIM ontology. This release freezes SSTIM 0.20.0, published at https://w3id.org/sstim under CC BY 4.0: 18 modules holding 182 OWL classes and 371 properties labelled in English, and 645 SKOS concepts in English, Italian, Portuguese and Spanish, with SHACL validation shapes, four conformance profiles (Kernel, Core, Core Plus, Full), qualified evidence assessments, exposure and ecosystem term modules, and 110 verified external mappings to Wikidata, MeSH, UBERON and SNOMED CT alongside term reuse from BFO, COB, IAO, OBI, PROV-O and W3C ORG. Every mapping is dereferenced at the authority that mints its identifier and carries dated provenance and the reason for its predicate. The version IRI https://w3id.org/sstim/0.20.0 resolves to the frozen artifacts this archive contains. The archive is the whole repository at its release tag: the ontology sources and their frozen snapshot, the Svelte application (Graph Navigator, SPARQL interface, Patch Studio, four selectable audio engines), the validation and release tooling, and the documentation and architecture decision records. Its public reference data include nine published sensory stimulation protocols, from the 40 Hz auditory response of 1981 to a randomized home-use trial of 2022, each encoded from its paper, citing it, and asserting no effect. Licensing is per artifact class, and the three licences above are not alternatives. Each governs a different part of this archive: Apache-2.0 the software, build tooling and JSON contracts; CC BY 4.0 the ontology, vocabulary, public RDF data and documentation; CC0 1.0 the synthetic reference audio. A file carrying its own notice is governed by that notice, and LICENSING.md in the archive is the scope matrix. Scope. Sensory stimulation spans self-directed practice through regulated clinical intervention, and SSTIM describes that whole range: electroconvulsive therapy, interventional neurostimulation and preclinical study designs are published terms. The Workbench itself is general wellness software rather than a medical device, and carries no diagnostic or treatment claim; that is a statement about this implementation, not about the field. Community Group work is not a W3C Recommendation and is not W3C-endorsed technology. Ecosystem fixtures in the release are synthetic; real live-only agent records are kept outside this archive by design. The Workbench's stakeholder directory does list real companies, laboratories, people and projects of the field, each from a public source: it is a listing of relevance, not an agent record, and an entry removed on request is absent from later releases only. Each tagged release is archived here for citation.
items.title: SSTIM Workbench: Open Sensory Stimulation Platform and SSTIM Ontology

items.summary: Classical inverse bandit methods typically aim to recover true reward parameters. In contrast, we infer a demonstrator's subjective beliefs, specifically its internal estimates of suboptimality gaps. We consider no-regret demonstrators that follow randomized policies, such as Thompson sampling, and characterize a family of algorithms for which per-step inversion is possible. This enables gap estimates to be recovered directly from the arm-selection distribution. Our analysis identifies an inherent stability-coverage trade-off: inversion becomes ill-conditioned as the demonstrator concentrates its probability mass on a single arm, while the number of informative rounds depends on the rate at which its policy converges. We establish conditions under which inversion is reliable and provide theoretical guarantees on the resulting estimation error. Experiments on simulated data support the analysis and illustrate how these conditions affect gap recovery in practice.
items.title: Learning from a Bandit Learner

Cohort, acquisition and games are inherited; the added contribution is an inspectable association between observations, original source indices, admitted recording windows, missingness and technical provenance, together with a bounded reuse example. items.summary: We study inverse coefficient problems for two evolution equations with relaxation: a Kelvin--Voigt viscoelastic equation and the Moore--Gibson--Thompson (MGT) equation arising in nonlinear acoustics. In both cases, we establish the Lipschitz stability for recovering a space-dependent coefficient from a single measurement. Our approach exploits an exact factorization of each operator into a classical evolution operator (the heat operator for the viscoelastic system, or the wave operator for the MGT equation) coupled with a first-order differential operator in time. This makes it possible to combine global Carleman estimates with weighted ODE inequalities. For the Kelvin--Voigt model, the data consist of an interior dynamic observation and a Cauchy snapshot at a prescribed positive time. For the MGT equation, a single boundary trace is sufficient under a standard geometric condition. The resulting argument provides a common framework for coefficient inverse problems in evolution equations with relaxation effects.

items.summary: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.
items.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability

items.summary: The macroscopic capabilities of intelligent systems arise from the local interactions of many simple units. When such systems are deployed in the real world, their behaviour must nevertheless be constrained, leaving designers caught between releasing adaptability and preventing loss of control, yet without formal tools to resolve the dilemma. This paper proposes a unified research program for controlled emergence that restates this tension as a pair of dual problems: the forward problem explains macroscopic behaviour from local rules, and the inverse problem solves for controllable rules and readout mechanisms from a desired target. We take an augmented quintuple as the formal object shared by both ends, and decompose ``engineering'' into three independently measurable coordinates: controllability, reproducibility, and degree of formalizability. On this basis we give three testable working hypotheses (critical scale; the cooperation and trade-off between constraint and adaptability; minimal constraint) and one feasibility criterion, which reduce inverse design from unconstrained optimization to interval checking. The program takes explicit failure boundaries as its premise, does not pursue complete control, and always preserves the system's room for self-organization. The reduced pilot experiment attached to this paper serves only to verify the executability of the research protocol and does not constitute a statistical test of the working hypotheses. This design language generalizes to multi-agent artificial intelligence, the industrial internet, and emergency response systems, all of which must confront emergence and controllability at once.
items.title: The Forward/Inverse Duality of Controlled Emergence:A Computational Design Program from Explanation to Engineering

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are trained through multi-stage pipelines over heterogeneous data sources, yet developers lack a principled way to pinpoint the specific data responsible for an observed behavior. This lack of observability reduces debugging to reactive patching and makes failures prone to recur under distribution shift or subsequent model updates. To address this limitation, we propose DebugLM, a framework that equips LLMs with built-in data provenance, enabling them to explicitly trace the origins of their behaviors to specific training data sources. Specifically, the model learns to associate its responses with unique provenance tags that indicate the responsible dataset, empowering developers to precisely identify where undesirable behaviors are learned. Building on this capability, DebugLM further supports targeted test-time remediation, enabling developers to selectively trigger targeted refusal for specified data sources without retraining or modifying model parameters. Experiments demonstrate that DebugLM provides accurate behavior tracing in multi-stage training pipelines and effective test-time remediation while preserving the general utility of the model.
items.title: DebugLM: Learning Traceable Training Data Provenance for LLMs

items.summary: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.
items.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?

items.summary: RECONFIGURABLE ROBOTIC SWARMS AND CONTINUOUS FUNCTIONAL REGENERATION AT THE LIMIT STARLI Research Works | White Rainbow Scientific Library | Flagship 02 Prospective Research Atlas — English Review Edition, October 2026 Can a distributed population of heterogeneous modular robots reconstruct an operationally qualified capability after damage, without treating a newly assembled shape as evidence of restored function? Reconfigurable Robotic Swarms and Continuous Functional Regeneration at the Limit develops an interdisciplinary research program on modular morphology, distributed self-assembly, task-dependent graph structure, mechanical qualification, connector fatigue, recoverable actions, and independent post-reconfiguration verification. Its central proposition is deliberately testable: a swarm may change its topology after losing modules, but it earns the stronger name of functional regeneration only when its restored configuration satisfies the original, independently assessed service requirements and does not conceal emerging hazards or latent joint failures. The monograph distinguishes three often conflated networks: mechanical connections that transmit forces, communication links that transmit information, and power connections that transport energy. It then investigates how graph connectivity, geometric rigidity, elastic stiffness, buckling, frictional contact, thermal dissipation, material fatigue, sensing uncertainty, local negotiation, and safe rollback constrain what an apparently repaired swarm can actually do. A prospective twenty-module testbed provides recurring engineering anchors: bridge, gripping, and sensing-tower tasks, blinded removal of modules, unseen configurations, independent qualification, and strong comparisons with redundant fixed structures and specialist replacement procedures. The research architecture includes thirty mathematically diverse derivation plates, eighty-two chapter-level questions and their five individually paginated study units, two hundred falsifiable Research Gates, and thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos. The companion spreadsheet links physical models, chapter topics, prospective study cards, provenance, source DOI records, and page references to support future research and AI-assisted scientific handoff. Published robotics literature supplies a source-grounded context for modular reconfigurable mechanisms and fault-aware planning, including external DOI records for reviews and an existing fault-tolerant modular system. The manuscript separates those precedents from its own unexecuted research designs. Its two STARLI mother volumes are listed as conceptual ancestry, not as independent experimental validation. Biological regeneration functions as an analogy for staged assessment of restoration, not as evidence of biomedical efficacy, autonomous human-tissue repair, or indefinite machine life. This is a prospective research-atlas REVIEW EDITION. The mathematical relations, study proposals, design seeds, and acceptance thresholds are not experimentally validated findings. External mathematical review, whole-text DOI auditing, and a stronger editorial review for chapter-level semantic repetition remain necessary before scholarly publication. Negative findings, conventional method superiority, irreversible module retirement, and scientific abstention are legitimate outcomes within this research program. items.summary: Autonomous clinical-modeling agents can optimize predictive performance while violating conditions that make a model usable. We introduce LeakBench, an executable, guideline-derived audit suite that tests agent decisions for prediction-time leakage, calibration, site-level evaluation, support awareness, and decision-curve net benefit. LeakBench combines a synthetic task with known failure structure and two real-data settings: MIMIC-IV (430k admissions) and governed multi-hospital inpatient record front-page (MHFP) data. Our primary analysis uses reward hacking descriptively, without attributing intent: an agent selects prediction-time-invalid inputs because they improve its validation reward. A deterministic optimizer and every evaluated unconstrained local-model configuration select a fatal leaking feature. In fully logged September 2026 A/B runs, DeepSeek Flash and GPT-6-astra each leak in 10/10 unconstrained runs and 0/10 runs with an explicit admission-time constraint. This contrast is version-sensitive: a blinded Claude/Fable-5.1 chat run does not leak in either condition, while explicit-constraint violations appear only in a historical August 2026 slice lacking raw trajectories. Replacing AUROC with AUPRC does not remove leakage selection. Renaming or disguising the leaking inputs changes neither selection nor provenance-based detection; a name-based filter fails. A deterministic provenance verifier-in-loop removes the leak, making the LLM repair loop defense-in-depth. Specific verifier feedback clears fatal leakage in a hosted agent, and a three-seed ablation finds principle-only feedback clears decision-level defects, though these mitigation results are limited. LeakBench treats trustworthy clinical prediction as a property of an agent's modeling process, not merely its score; it is an audit testbed with known-failure controls, not yet an expert-validated benchmark.
items.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents

items.summary: Assembly traces can support explicit probabilistic inference without being treated as recovered program meaning. Active Assembly Theory and Practice makes that distinction executable: transparent x86-64 fixtures are decoded with Capstone, traced under bounded Unicorn emulation, and mapped to typed observations that distinguish missing, unseen, and unsupported evidence. Two Generalized Notation Notation (GNN) specifications define passive-phase and prospective sensor models whose tensors drive real pymdp execution. A native categorical Julia/RxInfer companion consumes the passive model's same parameters (Friedman 2026; Heins et al. 2022; Bagaev et al. 2023). The sensor Agent selects an action before fixture evidence is acquired. Independent finite calculations check beliefs and policy scores; native smoothing uses the same parameters and first-observation convention. Every inference comparator and fitted diagnostic also consumes an upstream-parsed numeric GNN specification, with source-bound runtime instances and rendered model graphs. A corpus of 10 authored fixtures supports complete-fixture exclusion diagnostics. At the fixed informative likelihood, the memoryless decoder outperforms the temporal filter; temporal advantages appear under synthetic observation ambiguity. Designed category ambiguity remains a visible failure case. The separate Gaussian and categorical Bethe free-energy diagnostics are not compared numerically with policy expected free energy. The quotient benchmark contains 64 transformation-family identifiers and 4096 rows, with 16 families held out from model fitting. The co-primary portfolio includes an interpretable classifier, a temporal probabilistic model, a fixed one-layer tanh recurrent classifier, and surface baselines; the temporal endpoint reaches balanced accuracy 0.775 and macro-F1 0.772 on this frozen bounded benchmark. Held-out identifiers share authored template lineages with the fitting data. Family-resampling intervals and conditional randomization diagnostics therefore describe this finite inventory; the retrospective protocol correction withholds superiority claims. A complementary pinned static-only corpus supplies 5 licensed source projects and 100 source-contract rows, including 40 lexical witnesses, 40 contract-directed near misses, and 20 identity controls. The corpus establishes provenance and coverage; it does not execute arbitrary external binaries or support application-effectiveness claims. Selected normalized machine-state relations are checked by Python, native execution, and a bounded Lean fragment. Exact finite sensing certificates and source-bound reader artifacts make assumptions and failures inspectable. Independent physical replication remains unearned. The contribution is a reproducible substrate for testing assembly-to-inference mechanisms, with explicit limits on semantics, statistical generalization, and external validity.

items.summary: Curated Wearable Physiological Signals for Paediatric ADHD Research, with Task-Aligned Data and EDA Baselines This resource organises existing Empatica EmbracePlus recordings from the BALLADEER paediatric ADHD study into source-traceable native task views, with optional full native context, descriptive quality control (QC) and processed electrodermal activity (EDA). Cohort, acquisition and games are inherited; the added contribution is an inspectable association between observations, original source indices, admitted recording windows, missingness and technical provenance, together with a bounded reuse example. Coverage and signals The inventory comprises 107 participants and five tasks : CogniFit (01), Attention Robots (02), and screen-based Attention Slackline levels 1, 6 and 11 (03–05). EDA overlaps admitted EEG recording spans for 436 participant/task combinations across 104 people , with 1,129,180 finite selected EDA samples . Of 535 possible EDA cells, 77 lack an EEG span and 22 have EEG but no EDA overlap. Availability and temporal overlap do not establish full-task coverage, physiological suitability or final analytical eligibility. The golden layer contains 37,974,199 native rows across supported streams. The complete native projection contains 228,120,776 rows, including 6,779,644 EDA rows with 20 untimed entries, and extends outside task windows. These representations overlap; do not sum them as independent observations or treat time-series samples/task rows as independent participants. Golden native stream Rows Quantity/unit Accelerometer 18,069,607 Three-axis int32 ADC counts; native calibration context retained BVP 18,067,914 Optical pulse waveform, writer-declared nW; not blood pressure EDA 1,129,180 Signed float32 µS Temperature 282,293 float32 °C Steps 56,461 Vendor int32 counts Systolic peaks 368,743 Vendor event times, original indices and UTC nanosecond source time Wearable tags 1 Native event time, original index and UTC microsecond source time Gyroscope 0 Supported schema, empty stream The single tag is not full-cohort coverage. Availability retains missing combinations explicitly. Participant metadata has exactly participant_id , age , gender and group . Identifiers remain strings; recorded gender is not renamed biological sex. Group 1/2 denotes experimental/ADHD recruitment and comparison under the approved interpretation, not assessment-derived diagnosis or uniformly healthy controls. Downloads and reassembly Logical archive Complete size Upload files golden_dataset.zip 606.25 MB 7 native_projection.zip 2955.75 MB 30 quality_control.zip 2.73 MB 1 processed_eda.zip 35.75 MB 1 baseline_reproduction.zip 18.89 MB 1 Each upload file is at most 100,000,000 bytes . Golden and native archives are byte-split into numbered parts; parts are not independently extractable ZIP files . Download all seven golden_dataset.zip.part001 – .part007 files for golden data, or all 30 native_projection.zip.part001 – .part030 files for the native supplement. The other three archives are ordinary single ZIPs. This size is a delivery choice, not a platform limit. Keep archive_registry.json and reassemble.py beside the desired complete part set. Run python3 reassemble.py verify --archive golden_dataset.zip , create a new output directory, then run python3 reassemble.py reassemble golden_dataset.zip --output-dir reassembled . The standard-library helper checks ordered part and complete-ZIP hashes, refuses overwrites and never extracts or runs analysis. Extract the verified ZIP with an ordinary tool into a new empty directory. Substitute the native archive name for that route. For a single ZIP, verify it by name and extract directly. README.md gives exact commands and reconstruction-space guidance. Golden data: primary native wearable task views/events, metadata, schemas, selection membership, QC and scientific provenance; independently usable after its parts are reassembled. Native projection: complete pr

items.summary: Recent advances in multimodal models have enabled GPT-6 Astra to perform robotic manipulation through in-context learning. Yet contact-rich control and tactile perception are often regarded as strengths of specialist policies, leaving open whether Astra can directly understand and use tactile observations. We provide, to our knowledge, the first demonstration that Astra directly interprets vision-based tactile images and uses their contact cues for manipulation. Tactile RGB images enter through its existing visual interface, enabling few-shot closed-loop control on nineteen simulated UniVTAC and OpenViTac tasks with 210 sampled scene seeds per setting. With visuo-tactile input, Astra achieves mean success rates of 93.8% and 81.8%, exceeding the strongest reported specialist baselines in our comparison by 22.9 and 13.1 percentage points, respectively. Vision-only performance also leads these baselines, reaching 76.3% and 80.6%. Trajectory analysis reveals active probing, cautious grasping, contact-guided alignment, and recovery, alongside difficulties with tangential loading and corrective execution. Our findings challenge the exclusivity of specialist policies in contact-rich manipulation and show that fine-grained vision can partially compensate for missing touch. They also identify vision-based tactile sensing as an interface for scaling contact understanding with foundation models and reveal signs of benchmark saturation. These results motivate joint visual-tactile pretraining, harder contact-rich evaluations, and physical-robot validation.
items.title: GPT-6 Astra Is a Native Visuo-Tactile Policy for Contact-Rich Manipulation

items.summary: Precomputed results for DOST (Distance-preserving Optimization for Spatial Transcriptomics), a method for identifying spatial domains in spatial transcriptomics data. This record accompanies the DOST code (see Related works) and the DOST paper. results.zip contains the outputs of the scripts in the reproducibility/ directory of the code repository, for DOST and for the baseline methods BANKSY, BASS, DR.SC, GraphST, STAGATE, SpaGCN, stCluster and ADEPT. These are the files read by the figure scripts in reproducibility/figures/ . To use the files, unzip results.zip , set dir.output in the figure scripts to the unzipped folder, and run the scripts as described in reproducibility/figures/README.md in the code repository. The datasets are not included. They are publicly available from the BenchmarkST Zenodo records (DLPFC12, BC, mMAMP and mHypothalamus) and from 10x Genomics (Xenium Human Breast); see reproducibility/DOST/README.md in the code repository.
items.title: Precomputed results for DOST reproducibility

items.summary: Version 2.3 of Adversarial Multi-AI Falsification is a bounded case study of AI-assisted scholarly workflow governance. It distinguishes selected public verbatim excerpts and message/line maps from author-reported recovery findings and hashes identifying internal artifacts. The public deposit does not contain the full captured transcripts or executed rubric. Four process-failure types required exclusion or downgrading: semantic drift with unsupported process certification; assignment-scope expansion; prior-task substitution; and unverified or misdescribed legal citations. E2 remains partial. The principal execution/adjudication sequence remains author-reconstructed, and panel unanimity cannot be independently recomputed from the public deposit. The operational proposition remains untested; this revision does not establish it as true. The paper proposes a three-field outcome record and six workflow controls, including a two-turn assignment-echo checkpoint. These are unvalidated design propositions, not demonstrated interventions. This is a case report and protocol demonstration, not a benchmark, product comparison, prevalence estimate or complete reproducibility study. AMAF_v2_3.pdf is the current controlling manuscript, with AMAF_v2_3.docx as its editable counterpart. All seven v2.2 files are retained unchanged as historical records, including the old preparation-candidate manuscript, README, manifest and checksum list. Read 00_README_AMAF_v2_3_RELEASE.txt for the current controlling-version guide; AMAF_v2_3_SHA256SUMS.txt lists this release's file identities. The historical v1.8 paper is retained only for its Section C dual-track summary. No additional private records, new experiment or new empirical validation are released. Generative AI systems were used for structured literature discovery, comparative issue mapping, adversarial review, source-check planning, language editing and revision support. They are not authors. The human author retains responsibility for the sources, interpretations, arguments and conclusions.
items.title: Adversarial Multi-AI Falsification in Research Workflows: A Bounded Case Study of Scope Error, Verification Failure, and Human Adjudication

items.summary: annotations4all is a schema-first Python library for LLM-assisted span annotation, including named entity recognition. Users define their own tag schemas; the library generates chat prompts, parses annotated model responses and maps annotations to character offsets in the original text. The library keeps annotation mechanics separate from research workflows: it bundles no corpus or fixed ontology, performs no evaluation, and does not promise model quality. Provider support uses explicit OpenAI-compatible routes rather than native SDKs. What the library provides Schema-first prompt generation and response parsing. Configurable taggers, German and English prompt templates, metadata-bearing spans and structured parser warnings. Per-label annotation and deterministic merge. Independent label runs can be combined using containment-derived hierarchy, explicit conflict reports and bounded anchoring. One request per run has a corresponding inference cost; merge is not a semantic error repair. Provider policies and capability evidence. A generic OpenAI-compatible client, provider-policy clients, explicit reasoning activation and effort, request limits, packaged hints and offline capability reports. Remote verification requires opt-in; metadata does not prove account access or successful inference. Optional read-only terminal viewer. Browse saved annotations, inspect nested spans and compare two sources using synchronized split or compact diff views. The viewer does not modify annotation files or run inference. Release notes 0.3.1 Request pacing now resolves symlinks in the parent directories of the per-user state file, so a symlinked cache root no longer fails every paced request. The state file keeps its no-follow, regular-file and ownership protection, and cross-process locking is unchanged. Documentation is available in both languages: tutorial and viewer guide each in German and English. Release 0.3.0 introduced provider-policy clients, capability reporting, the optional viewer, data-dependent contrast optimization and deprecation warnings for the legacy native wrappers; the 0.3 notes remain the reference for that feature set. 0.3.1 release notes ; 0.3 feature release notes and screenshots ; initial 0.2 feature baseline . Installation, documentation and verification Python 3.11 or newer. Install with pip install annotations4all==0.3.1 ; add the optional viewer with pip install 'annotations4all[view]==0.3.1' . The tutorial in German and English, the API guides, release notes and screenshot provenance are included with the source archive. Verification: 984 passing tests, 92.8% coverage, Ruff lint/format checks, warning-free Markdownlint, package metadata checks and fresh-environment installation tests under Python 3.11 and 3.13. Viewer checks include real optimization subprocesses and terminal restoration. These are code and packaging checks, not live-provider benchmarks. Versioning, license and citation Version 0.3.1 . MIT license. The source archive includes machine-readable CITATION.cff metadata. Version DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23494842 . The unchanged concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22011370 identifies the software across versions. Source code and issues ; Python package .
